ai.title: Can AI automate Epoch?
ai.summary: Epoch Automation Reports show that models can't yet autonomously produce Epoch-quality work. Frontier models performed reliably on well-defined tasks, but they failed in the more open-ended aspects that prevent full automation. Open-weight models lag further behind, struggling even on the well-defined tasks that frontier models handle reliably. The models struggle to pick up Epoch's standards, even with ample reference material, and while they could identify promising research directions, they lacked the judgment to successfully follow through.

ai.title: Why is Speculative Decoding Fast?
ai.summary: Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.

ai.title: ATLAS: Evaluating Agents on Search-Intensive Tasks

ATLAS differs from existing benchmarks by focusing on non-memorized tasks, requiring extensive multi-domain searches, and offering a cost-effective grading process.

webdev.title: When code is cheap, judgement becomes the job
webdev.summary: As AI makes code production cheap, the scarce work shifts to choosing priorities, reviewing product behavior, maintaining architecture, and owning outcomes in production. Senior engineers create leverage by turning repeated review feedback into guidance and deterministic lint rules while keeping human judgment for business context.

webdev.title: Don't merge what you didn't run: a test gate for agent-written code
webdev.summary: A practical test gate checks agent-written changes on a clean machine before review by reinstalling from scratch, running the full suite three times, rejecting removed or skipped tests, and restoring the base branch's tests against the new code. Running the same gate inside the agent loop turns failures into immediate repair instructions while an independent CI run keeps the verdict outside the agent's control.

webdev.title: Treg

webdev.title: Plannotator

webdev.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server
webdev.summary: A React Server Components flaw let an attacker force quadratic work while React rebuilt FormData for a server action, allowing a roughly 900 KB request to trigger 100 million string checks and block a Node.js event loop. The issue affects vulnerable React 19.0 to 19.2 releases and is fixed in 19.0.6, 19.1.7, and 19.2.6.

webdev.title: Your skills need an evaluation mechanism
webdev.summary: Expo built a CI evaluation harness that measures whether coding agents discover relevant skills, follow their guidance, and produce working apps. infosec.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised: A Worm With a Hostage Token That Wipes Your Machine If You Revoke It
infosec.summary: tensorlake@0.5.144 on npm steals developer credentials at install and plants a gh-token-monitor service that wipes the home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked. The release was built from malicious commits pushed straight to the project's main branch under a maintainer's name, StepSecurity found, so it carries a valid npm provenance attestation while spreading through victims' npm packages and repos. Pin to 0.5.143, remove the service under ~/.config/gh-token-monitor/ before revoking any token, then rotate every credential the machine held.

infosec.title: Cisco Warns of Critical Flaws Allowing Nexus Switch Takeover
infosec.summary: Cisco announced security advisories for five critical vulnerabilities in its NX-OS data center operating system that could allow remote code execution on Nexus switches. Successful exploitation depends on the NX-API, Next Generation OAM, and MPLS OAM features being enabled. Cisco recommends disabling these features if they aren't necessary and upgrading to a patched version.

infosec.title: Poetry is the new AI security threat as PoeLLM malware infects 3K+ servers
infosec.summary: The PoeLLM malware has infected more than 3,000 servers since April, primarily in the US and Western Europe. It targets internet-facing LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, and possibly Ivanti Sentry systems. Infected servers mine Monero using XMRig and Iron miners, then scan for and exploit other vulnerable services. The operator stores C2 addresses in GitHub-hosted poetry. The malware extracts four words and converts them into an IPv4 address.

infosec.title: Novinarya: An Android stealer that hides its live C2 in a shop bio
infosec.summary: Novinarya, an Android stealer targeting 81 Iranian banking and crypto apps, keeps its C2 out of the binary by resolving it from an encrypted manifest value that points to a seller's bio on the legitimate Basalam marketplace. STAR Labs found the payload unpacks from a per-build native RC4 packer, then steals credentials through a phishing WebView and SMS OTP interception without requesting accessibility or overlay permissions. Defenders should block the recovered C2 (theapi.the-x-services[.]xyz) rather than basalam[.]com, and detect on the SHA-256 hashes of the unpacked payload, which is byte-identical across all five known builds.

infosec.title: Of course it escapes: how ZeroQuarry contains security agents
infosec.summary: ZeroQuarry's AI pentesting agents use four layers that never depend on the model's cooperation: outbound-only workers with no listener, a locked-down container, tools that enforce scope, SSRF, and rate limits in code, and rules appended to every task by code. The vendor argues that this year's sandbox escapes, including the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident involving at least 1,200 agents, stemmed from harnesses built to maximize capability, and it self-reports zero escapes across thousands of scans. Teams building agent harnesses should give agents a sanctioned, metered tool for each risky action, such as a one-way out-of-band callback collector, so agents don't improvise their own.

infosec.title: Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware
infosec.summary: Malware authors are embedding plaintext instructions for AI analysis tools, ranging from a two-line comment claiming a PowerShell reverse shell is harmless to "template spraying" that repeats a refusal demand across seven LLM chat formats. Cisco Talos tested strings from seven families against five local LLMs and found that a simple, direct instruction steered verdicts toward benign in about 35% of runs, while template spraying and fabricated legal or government claims had little effect or backfired. Defenders should build analysis prompts that treat any text inside a sample as evidence rather than as an instruction, and should flag language addressed to an analyzer as a detection signal.

infosec.title: 7 best practices for secrets lifecycle management
infosec.summary: From agents to service accounts, non-human identities are becoming the default - and their secrets are a major attack surface. TruffleHog's guides shares seven best practices to limit exposure and remediate it when it happens: secretless OIDC approaches, environment segregation, metadata-driven triage, resilient leak response, and more. Watch their webinar on the attacker's view of a leaked AWS key here.

infosec.title: Rein Security (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: Rein Security provides runtime security for AI agents. Its platform gives visibility into agent behavior, applies real-time guardrails, supports governance, and includes supply-chain security for agents.

infosec.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
infosec.summary: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that sends open-source maintainers periodic vulnerability reports from its most capable models, each with a proof of concept and a suggested fix where available. Reports ship without human review at what Anthropic estimates is a 90%+ true-positive rate, so the service targets projects with the capacity to triage. The same announcement introduced the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, which pairs Claude models and on-site engineers with OT security providers including Dragos, Nozomi Networks, and Rockwell Automation.

infosec.title: Introducing Strands Box: AI agent sandboxes powered by Dogwood
infosec.summary: AWS launched Strands Box, an open source sandbox that isolates AI agents using OS-level containment (macOS Seatbelt) and enforces fine-grained Dogwood policies on shell, Python, network egress, and MCP tools. It blocks risky operations like rm -rf by raising fs:delete decisions per file, caps Slack posts to three every 10 minutes via temporal rules, and injects secrets (AWS SigV4, API keys) at an egress gateway so agents never see real credentials. Configuration lives in box.toml and policy.dw. The same policy travels with agents across harnesses and deployments.

infosec.title: Ransomware Recovery CEO Charged Over Secret Ransom Payments
infosec.summary: Zohar Pinhasi, CEO of ransomware remediation company MonsterCloud, has been charged with defrauding customers. The charges allege that Pinhasi's company advertised proprietary tools to decrypt encrypted files but actually contacted ransomware actors and paid ransoms. MonsterCloud's contracts stated that it may contact threat actors if no other solution is found, but the complaint alleges this was often its first option.

infosec.title: CIA officer admits to creating fake top secret government program to steal over $190M, including gold bars
infosec.summary: Former CIA officer David J. Rush pleaded guilty to wire fraud for running a fabricated special access program and defrauding the government of about $194 million. He used his authority to approve spending without oversight, tricking a defense contractor into buying gold that he kept. Agents found $46 million in gold bars, plus cash, cars, and watches, at his home. Rush faces up to 20 years and is scheduled to be sentenced in late January.

infosec.title: Oracle Health Data Breach Tally Climbs to Nearly 20 Million
infosec.summary: A cyberattack on Oracle Health's legacy Cerner servers around February 20, 2025, exposed the personal and medical data of nearly 20 million people. The attacker used stolen customer credentials to access an old server not yet migrated to Oracle Cloud, copied data, and then demanded millions in cryptocurrency from hospitals while running public sites to pressure victims.

infosec.summary: Let's Encrypt will cut certificate lifetimes from 90 to 64 days on February 10, with opt-in testing from October 14 and 45-day defaults planned for 2028, which will break renewals that run on hardcoded schedules instead of ACME ARI.

devops.summary: The DNS root is scheduled to switch to KSK-2024 on October 11, and DNSSEC-validating resolvers that lack the new trust anchor could fail to resolve otherwise healthy websites. RFC 8509 sentinel queries let operators check readiness, although an unsupported sentinel test produces an inconclusive result rather than proving the key is missing.

devops.title: Kubelet watches inodes. Just not until it's an emergency
devops.summary: Kubelet's background image garbage collection only monitors disk bytes, so workloads heavy on small files receive no early intervention before kubelet evicts pods. On one node, unpacked layers from a single-stage build containing the @mui/icons-material package consumed millions of inodes. A multi-stage Dockerfile can reduce the deployed image from more than 40,000 files to a few dozen. Adding a Prometheus alert for inode usage above 80% can catch the problem well before the 95% eviction threshold.

devops.title: Beyond synthetic testing: Capturing and replaying real database workloads at Airbnb

devops.title: What is Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST)?

It suits QA and staging but needs runtime agents, adds overhead, and scales poorly across microservices, so mature programs pair it with SAST and SCA.

Meet the infrastructure for AI innovation in finance.

product.summary: While current AI agents act as standalone tools, future agents can develop network effects through acquisition and engagement loops. By turning artifacts into viral objects and building centralized identity layers, agent platforms could create winner-take-all dynamics.

product.title: Your Moat Is Dead. Anyone Can Rebuild Your Product
product.summary: Falling code generation costs and AI agent reimplementations have eliminated traditional software feature and UI moats. Defensibility has shifted toward accountability, proprietary data, regulatory trust, hardware coupling, and customer outcomes, forcing companies to focus on operational moats and server-side APIs.

product.title: Tesler's Law: complexity moved to a different part of the journey
product.summary: Generative AI interfaces do not eliminate software complexity - they shift it to users, developers, and reviewers. While AI automates routine tasks, it adds hidden burdens in prompt specification and verification. Designers must address this by creating clear constraints and verification workflows.

product.title: Why Agent-Written Code Needs Product Verification
product.summary: When AI agents write both code and tests, they encode identical misunderstandings, producing green builds that fail real user needs. Teams must establish independent verification based on user requirements. Lower maintenance costs and faster repair cycles make comprehensive end-to-end product verification feasible.

product.title: 4 free Datadog resources to help you understand your users
product.summary: Juggling tools to try and get a sense of your UX? This PM Toolkit by Datadog shows you how to extract real meaning from product data and build stronger pre-launch hypotheses. Learn how to visually replay user sessions to uncover friction and prioritize updates that move the needle. Get the toolkit

product.title: Product definition
product.summary: Product thinking and "Product Definition" are essential in the AI era, where agents execute code rapidly given clear direction. Formerly known as feature specification, Product Definition shapes requirements and context into actionable artifacts like prototypes and PRDs. This competency evolves from tactical execution to building systems that align teams and AI agents.

product.title: When Does Onboarding Become a Product Problem?
product.summary: Customer onboarding friction often signals a hidden product issue. Product managers should address this by creating a repeatable "Golden Path," mapping user tasks from purchase to production to replace manual steps with automated features. Tracking time to first value and completion rates reduces delays and builds long-term product value.

product.title: Introducing: Spotify Technology. Proven at Spotify, now yours
product.summary: Spotify Technology is a unified suite of developer and media tools including Portal, Confidence, Xirp, and Spotify for Backstage. Tested across Spotify's internal engineering teams to cover the entire development lifecycle, the offering aims to help external R&D organizations balance team autonomy with architectural alignment.

product.title: How Snyk turned an internal support agent into a customer feature
product.summary: Snyk turned its internal AI support agent, Snyk Assist, into a customer-facing feature. The agent answers user queries within permission boundaries, utilizing offline and online evaluations. Since launch, it has resolved over 85% of support sessions without needing a ticket.

product.title: Product Manager, Applied AI at TLDR ($225k base + $60k bonus, Fully Remote)
product.summary: TLDR is hiring its first PM to help build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has shipped real products/systems with LLMs. Click here to learn more .

product.title: Earn your MBA 100% online from The Ohio State University
product.summary: Advance your career with Ohio State's online MBA for Working Professionals-our nationally ranked part-time MBA with the flexibility of an online program that can be completed from anywhere. Explore the program

product.title: The most common reasons why AI pilots fail, even at the 'best' companies
product.summary: This thread outlines thirteen common pitfalls that cause enterprise AI pilots to fail, such as automating isolated steps instead of full workflows, lacking baseline metrics, ignoring edge cases, and failing to engage legal and security teams early.

product.title: What happens when AI agents shop for us
product.summary: As AI shopping agents use wallets to browse catalogs and complete checkouts automatically, online merchants risk losing direct customer contact, while users must retain final purchase approval to prevent accidental transactions.

design.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface
design.summary: OpenAI's Intelligent UI lets ChatGPT combine text with interactive diagrams, charts, buttons, and task-specific tools instead of using the same format for every answer. Users can explore explanations, change inputs, or use a calculator directly within a conversation, with the layout adapting to the question. The feature is rolling out with GPT-6 across paid and free plans, and users can reduce visual elements when they prefer simpler responses.

design.title: Google Releases Nano Banana 2.1 for Image Generation and Editing
design.summary: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 reached the Gemini API for image generation and editing, at 1K, 2K, and 4K resolutions. Google reports better text rendering, prompt adherence, and character consistency across successive edits, plus fixes for tiling artifacts in wide and panoramic images at 2K and 4K. The model is available as gemini-nano-banana-2.1, and Google has deprecated gemini-3.1-flash-image without announcing a shutdown date.

design.title: ChatGPT can imitate a cartoonist. Now it's signing their name, too
design.summary: ChatGPT has generated cartoons containing signatures associated with more than 15 New Yorker contributors, potentially making AI-generated work appear to have been created by real artists. Cartoonists including Brendan Loper and Emily Flake have encountered images bearing recognizable versions of their names despite having no involvement in creating them. OpenAI has introduced warnings for some New Yorker-style requests, but signed outputs have reportedly continued to appear, raising concerns that style imitation can cross into false attribution.

design.title: Imperfection
design.summary: A personal website redesign became an excuse to explore deliberately playful details, including fake game cartridges for past jobs, draggable photo prints, paper-like shaders, animated labels, unusual links, and dynamically generated social cards. Many of these touches serve little practical purpose, but that lack of optimization is precisely what makes the process enjoyable and gives the site its personality. Personal projects can create space for experimentation that professional work often removes, making unnecessary details, imperfection, and prolonged tinkering valuable in themselves.

design.title: Slack Content Design in the Age of AI
design.summary: Slack's AI-drafted UI copy is almost indistinguishable from human work, and content designers are uniquely equipped to close the trust gap that "almost" opens. When Slackbot appeared to leak private information that was actually hallucinated, the team redesigned the UX to fetch correct data and explain why LLMs hallucinate. Three tenets guide the work: trust is the product, human judgment is irreplaceable, and language is infrastructure for AI agents.

design.title: Building a General-Purpose Accessibility Agent—and What We Learned in the Process
design.summary: An experimental general-purpose accessibility agent piloted at GitHub has reviewed 3,535 pull requests with a 68% resolution rate. It gives engineers real-time guidance in Copilot CLI and VS Code, and fixes straightforward issues before code reaches production. A parent agent directs two sub-agents, a passive reviewer and an active implementer, and escalates drag-and-drop, data grids, and rich text editors to human specialists.

design.title: Any Website's Design, as a Prompt for Your AI
design.summary: A Safari extension for Mac that measures any website's colors, type, spacing, and layout, then hands it to your coding agent as one measured prompt.

design.title: Energy Icons — energy transition icons
design.summary: Energy Icons is an open-source library of more than 1,200 icons for energy and climate products, covering areas such as renewables, electricity, transportation, buildings, and decarbonization in two optical sizes and two weights.

design.title: Create Physical Products
design.summary: Create physical products with Autonomyware: everyday objects, complex systems, sculpts, and toys, engineered autonomously from your idea.

design.title: Testing the iPad Air M4 as a multi-disciplinary artist: does it stack up?
design.summary: The M4 iPad Air's 12GB of unified memory brings it much closer to the iPad Pro for demanding creative work, comfortably handling large Procreate files, 3D models approaching 20 million polygons, and ProRes video editing. Its M4 chip delivers roughly 42% higher single-core and 44% higher multi-core Geekbench performance than the M2 Air, while Apple Pencil Pro support provides the same drawing experience as higher-end models. The iPad Pro still offers advantages such as an OLED display, nano-texture glass, and more memory, but many artists, illustrators, 3D artists, photographers, and video editors may no longer need to pay the premium.

design.title: Mother Design exercises restraint with new M&S pack system
design.summary: Mother Design has created a restrained packaging system for thousands of M&S Home and Lingerie products by removing competing sub-brands and hierarchies and looking to classic information design rather than other retailers for inspiration. The system standardizes MS London typography, introduces a geometric numeral set called MS London Geo, and uses grids, consistent hierarchy, restrained colors, and color-coded sizing to make complex product information easier to navigate. Packaging materials, photography, and tone adapt between Home and Lingerie while maintaining a shared structure designed to strengthen the M&S master brand and scale into additional categories.

design.title: Street Artist Turns Graffiti Letters into Neon Portals Where Typography, Architecture, and Science Fiction Collide
design.summary: Spanish artist Javier Demsky, who started in graffiti in the early 1990s, bends the letters of his name into luminous structures blending typography, architecture, and science fiction.

design.title: Information Architecture Works at Different Scales
design.summary: Evaluating an information architecture starts with its scale, whether organization, platform, site, interface, or interaction, since only IAs at the same scale can be compared.

marketing.title: Big Tech is cutewashing its AI agents
marketing.summary: Cuteness triggers the brain's pleasure centers before conscious thought, which makes people want to keep cute things close and more willing to forgive their mistakes. That makes big-eyed mascots a useful wrapper for AI agents that still hallucinate and need mass adoption. The same move made the early internet feel less intimidating in the late 1990s, then faded once the technology became routine. However, a look shared by every major AI company stops identifying any one of them and can become shorthand for what people distrust about the industry.

marketing.title: Building better public signals for AI impacts
marketing.summary: Analysis of 137,000 r/ChatGPT posts shows how users' experiences and expectations changed as ChatGPT became part of everyday life. Posts about therapy and companionship increased after the release of GPT-4o in May 2024 and reached about 10% of subreddit posts, while discussion of prompting declined as users became more familiar with AI. The researchers' real-time monitoring system could have detected the rise in emotional engagement by October 2024, months before broader discussion of sycophancy and AI psychosis. The findings suggest that Reddit can reveal emerging patterns in AI use and potential societal impacts that may not appear in traditional usage data.

marketing.title: 6 steps to building fast landing pages
marketing.summary: Instead of waiting weeks for overloaded web teams to build campaign pages, build lean landing pages in Claude Code and get them into market quickly. Start with a clear conversion problem, then write a 7-line brief and give AI a reusable context file covering brand voice, product details, customer language, and design rules. Ship at 70-80% polish while validating high-risk copy. Have stakeholders review a live preview, then hand off the approved page as a launch-ready bundle. If it performs, the web team rebuilds it properly.

marketing.title: 5 Things Content Marketers & SEOs Should Stop Doing in 2026
marketing.summary: Zero-click search has made five common content habits counterproductive. Building pages around keywords misses how people now query, since the average ChatGPT prompt runs 23 words. Grading content on traffic ignores that the top-ranked page loses 58% of its CTR under an AI Overview. Publishing more matters less than maintaining what exists, as 75% of AI-cited pages were updated in the past year. The last two are relying on owned channels, when 85% of AI brand mentions come from third parties, and publishing generic guides with no original data.

marketing.title: The Reason to Be on Reddit isn't for AEO
marketing.summary: Reddit is more valuable as a mid-funnel research channel than an AEO play because developers use it to compare tools and real-world experiences before buying. Treat it like earned media by joining existing conversations without pitching. Build credibility for about 3 months before approaching moderators about AMAs or sponsored events. Focus posts on problems and lessons rather than products. Brand accounts can work when they consistently teach. Measure impact through customer interviews since Reddit influence rarely appears in analytics.

marketing.title: Google Search Data on Crawling, Indexing & Serving Timelines
marketing.summary: Google shared new internal data on how long crawling, indexing, and serving processes typically take. New URLs take about 20 hours to be discovered while known URLs take about 30 days to refresh. End-to-end indexing takes about 1.5 hours when processes run normally but can stretch to months or never. Title and snippet updates typically take 1-2 days, while site moves take 1-3 months. Core update recovery can take 3-6 months. Delays can stack because each process depends on the ones before it.

marketing.title: Lifecycle Live Workshop: Mapping the Customer Journey (Virtual Event)
marketing.summary: Phi Pham and Carlos Govantes will break down a real customer journey to identify friction and gaps across channels. You'll then map part of your own journey, such as signup to purchase or trial to paid. The workshop provides frameworks, prompts, tools, and live feedback to identify what to improve next.

marketing.title: How We Catch Messaging Campaign Drift Before It Spreads
marketing.summary: Campaign drift happens when the messages a business sends shift away from what was approved. This system for SMS and RCS converts each message into an embedding and matches it against clusters of previously judged traffic. Unmatched messages are grouped into new clusters, and an LLM issues one verdict per cluster against the approved campaign details rather than per message. Human reviewers confirm or override each flag before a sender is notified, restricted, or blocked.

marketing.title: How Wrong Is Your Marketing Mix Model (MMM)?
marketing.summary: MMM becomes more reliable when media budgets are deliberately phased, so channels move independently and spend reaches different levels. Build variation into the media plan by using tactics like weekly budget changes, dark periods, and peak spend periods instead of relying on model changes to solve weak data. In the simulation, the combined approach cut variance by 70% and bias by 47% while keeping each channel's annual budget unchanged. The tradeoff was a 3.42% loss in channel-driven revenue, so use lighter phasing when that cost is too high.

marketing.title: Desktop Habits Hide Mobile Friction
marketing.summary: Common sources of mobile friction that are missed by operators who only access the site on desktop.

marketing.title: Audiobooks on Spotify Are Going Global
marketing.summary: Spotify is expanding audiobook access from 22 to 180+ markets by the end of 2026.

marketing.title: Amazon's “About You” feature draws attention over detailed customer inferences
marketing.summary: Check Amazon's “About You” profile to see what the company has inferred about you.

founders.title: Make business money move faster
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Instead of stitching together separate systems, your team can manage more financial workflows on the platform you already use for payments. That means less time navigating disconnected tools and more time focused on your business. From everyday operations to your next stage of growth, Stripe Treasury gives you flexible infrastructure to move money faster, streamline how work gets done, and build financial operations that can adapt as you scale. Explore Stripe Treasury

founders.title: The Infinite SaaS Factory
founders.summary: Microsoft has announced more than 30 new Copilot skills across Dynamics 365 Sales, Service, and Customer Insights, allowing users to use Copilot across Chat, Cowork, Autopilot, and Code to complete even more end-to-end workflows. Microsoft has also introduced Microsoft Copilot Managed Runtime, which provides hosting infrastructure that lets code run safely inside a company's environment, governed by IT. Together, these new tools start to form what the company envisions as an infinite SaaS factory.

founders.title: You Need a New CFO
founders.summary: AI-driven tools are transforming the CFO role, shifting focus from data management to strategic business architecture. Finance teams, now leaner and equipped with AI-native software, are evolving toward continuous forecasting and automated workflows. This change allows CFOs to prioritize real-time decision-making, enhancing their strategic influence within companies.

founders.title: References are the most underrated tool in hiring
founders.summary: By the time you're calling references on a candidate you want to hire, it can be hard to change your mind. This hiring guide starts the calls after the second interview, with the candidate's permission, and spreads them through the process. Build ten questions about what you still need to know for this particular role. Ask for stories and comparisons with other colleagues instead of adjectives like smart or hardworking. The answers can shape the next interview, including which claims to test. If a reference suggests another person to call, get the candidate's permission first.

founders.title: Marketing Engineers: 100x More Experiments with AI agents
founders.summary: Marketing engineers are the new 10x employee. Part marketers, part builders, marketing engineers understand the customer the best and can act on this understanding the fastest. The best marketing teams in the future will be one or two marketing engineers running dozens of agents. Most people sitting in growth, content, and ops roles right now are one weekend of billing away from becoming a marketing engineer. This post provides a full playbook on how to become one.

founders.title: Product Definition
founders.summary: Product definition is the ability to define requirements, functionality, and context in a clear, actionable form that enables humans and agents to deliver the right product. It involves getting the right product built well, understanding the people you build for, choosing the outcomes that matter, and rallying people around the organization to make things happen. The foundation of successful product management is the ability to work with a cross-functional team to define, build, and launch well-designed, stable products. The best product builders strive to execute flawlessly.

founders.title: Selling is human. Clarify runs the rest. 🏃‍♀️
founders.summary: Clarify is the full-stack AI CRM: CRM, prospecting, enrichment, reporting, and call intelligence in one system. Agents prep your meetings, log your calls, and find your next leads, so you pay for one tool instead of five. Free to start. Start for free

founders.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
founders.summary: Run high-volume summarization, classification, coding, support, and browser tasks efficiently.

founders.title: Ultrafast mode
founders.summary: OpenAI has released an API service tier for latency-sensitive work. Ultrafast mode is now broadly available for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. It has separate rate limits from Standard and Fast modes. Ultrafast is best suited for tasks where speed justifies a higher cost.

founders.title: Introducing the Gemini agent
founders.summary: The Gemini agent is a single, universal agent for work. It can gather all of a user's business context to complete tasks from knowledge work to answering questions, and from content creation to coding, all from a single prompt box. The agent plans the work, uses skills and tools, connects to systems, and returns something finished. It chooses the best model for the job and has built-in cost controls. The Gemini agent is able to follow security, administration, and governance policies set by the company.

founders.title: AI Versus Vendor Lock-in
founders.summary: Lock-in persisted for a long time because leaving was too expensive and risky. AI changed the cost of migrations. It's now possible to build a purpose-made converter, reimplement the behavior the business depends on, and use agents to move both code and data across. Businesses now have the ability to leave when the cost of staying gets too high.

founders.title: Compute Capital Markets
founders.summary: Compute is the fastest-growing asset class in the world. The demand for compute will likely continue to increase. Supply will remain constrained across chips, memory, power, and data center infrastructure. A new universe of productive financial assets is emerging, which means there will inevitably be robust markets to price, finance, and hedge exposures around the underlying. There is an immense opportunity in building a marketplace with embedded financial primitives to allow producers and consumers of compute to rigorously express risk preferences along the price and availability curve. These new capital markets are uniquely suited for crypto rails.

founders.title: The AI monetization debate shifts again
founders.summary: Paying salespeople on customer usage can reward growing existing accounts over finding new ones, so this guide explains how to add payments for new customers and reconcile estimated commissions against actual usage.

founders.title: Your Moat Is Dead. Anyone Can Rebuild Your Product.
founders.summary: A team created PhotoCraft, a Rust-based open-source clone of Photoshop, highlighting how easily feature-based software can be replicated.

founders.title: Lessons from Building AI Systems, Products, Startups
founders.summary: Lessons from getting AI products into customers' hands, including why better technology can be hard to sell and when an early customer's requests are turning your startup into a consulting business.

founders.title: AI Cognitive Atrophy
founders.summary: AI reliance leads to cognitive atrophy, as seen in professionals using LLMs to solve problems without critical thinking, reducing accountability and ownership.

founders.title: The Next Great Platform Shift: Personal Agents
founders.summary: Every previous platform shift changed how humans navigated interfaces - the personal agent removes the human from the interface altogether.

crypto.title: Standard Chartered to expand crypto custody services in Singapore
crypto.summary: Standard Chartered's Singapore unit plans to offer institutional custody for selected crypto assets, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets by the end of the year, subject to regulatory requirements. It extends the bank's existing custody footprint in the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong, and follows its move to bring Zodia Custody, the institutional custodian it incubated with Northern Trust, in-house.

crypto.title: Justin Drake Calls for Crypto "Bunker Mode" as AI Threatens ECDSA
crypto.summary: Ethereum researcher Justin Drake issued a call for "bunker mode," urging crypto holders to migrate assets to fresh addresses whose public keys remain hidden behind a hash before a potential ECDSA break. AI-driven mathematical progress, including OpenAI's recent mathematical superintelligence release and a series of proofs disproving long-held conjectures, may enable fast private key recovery on GPU clusters within months. Elliptic curves carry rich algebraic structure exploitable through AI-discovered techniques, and the absence of cryptographic breakthroughs among OpenAI's 722 published mathematical results raises the possibility of government-suppressed cryptanalysis. The Ethereum roadmap already targets hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification, and Drake is pushing to accelerate those timelines, while advising oracles and L2 security councils to rotate ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message.

crypto.title: Polygon Open Money Stack expands to TRON
crypto.summary: Polygon Labs announced its Open Money Stack now supports TRON, letting fintechs and remittance providers connect bank funds to USDT on TRON through one integration covering regulated ramps in 48 US states, programmable TRON wallets, and cross-chain routing between TRON and EVM networks. Polygon says it has processed over $3 trillion in payments volume, and the stack was assembled through its pending Coinme acquisition and its Sequence acquisition.

crypto.title: Reap can make almost any asset spendable with a regular card
crypto.summary: Reap Virtual Assets lets card projects make BTC, tokenized stocks and gold, yield-bearing assets, points, or even credit lines spendable by setting a fixed price or live price feed per asset and combining several into one card balance. The assets stay with the project while Visa settlement happens in USDC or USDT on the backend.

crypto.title: Vitalik on AI-Accelerated Cryptography: Hash-Based Over Lattices
crypto.summary: Vitalik Buterin warns that AI-accelerated mathematical research may erode the security of lattice-based cryptography (ML-DSA, LWE, and FHE) through the same mechanism that GNFS degraded RSA, where decades of optimization shrunk effective key strength by an order of magnitude, and projects that AI could compress 50 years of math progress into two years. Ethereum's lean roadmap has already pivoted to hash-only signatures (WOTS and SPHINCS+), dropping lattices, ML-DSA, Falcon, and lattice-based commitments from ZK proofs. Public-key encryption cannot be constructed from hashes alone due to long-standing mathematical constraints, which means secure messaging, VPNs, and anonymizing protocols face an open problem that extends well beyond blockchains. Buterin's practical recommendations include keeping funds in addresses that have not yet broadcast transactions, moving multisig confirmations offchain to avoid exposing signer public keys, and routing encrypted notes through offchain channels rather than publishing them onchain.

crypto.title: The Agentic Finance Landscape Report: Q3 2026 Edition
crypto.summary: Robinhood, eToro, Webull, and Coinbase all launched agentic trading accounts in Q3 2026, with Robinhood reporting 100K+ users and Coinbase securing the first SEC registration for an agentic investment adviser. x402 processed 232M transactions totaling $54M in volume, ERC-8004 agent registrations doubled quarter-over-quarter to 500K across 22 networks, and distributed RWA value reached $38.6B in Q3. Twenty-one major banks, including Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and Citi, committed to forming a stablecoin company, Mastercard launched Agent Pay for Machines with 30+ partners, including Coinbase and Stripe, and Visa cited x402 and MPP as better suited to machine-native micropayments than cards. Singapore's MAS released the SAFR framework for AI agents in finance co-authored by Circle, Visa, HSBC, and JPMorgan, while the US CLARITY Act failed a Senate vote, leaving the SEC and CFTC to establish crypto regulatory rules.

crypto.title: Morpho's fee switch is not comparable to Uniswap's
crypto.summary: Morpho's fee would have to come from suppliers (lowering yield on portable capital), curators (compressing margins and pushing them toward riskier vaults or other platforms like Aave V4), or both, unlike Uniswap, where liquidity benefits from the volume it attracts. Morpho still needs to prove pricing power, noting that Uniswap's recent strength came from an outlier month driven by Robinhood meme speculation, with volume now down about 71% from its September peak.

crypto.title: Crypto industry split over Justin Drake's AI warning
crypto.summary: Coinbase's head of cryptography Yehuda Lindell called Drake's warning that ECDSA could break within months "FUD," saying there is no evidence the hardness assumptions behind elliptic-curve cryptography have weakened. Dragonfly's Haseeb Qureshi called it "a very sober call," while Solana Foundation's Jacob Creech said Solana users do not need "bunker mode" because its Ed25519 setup could migrate to a quantum-resistant scheme through a hash-based proof.

crypto.title: BitMine Will Stop Buying ETH at 5% of Supply
crypto.summary: BitMine held 6,016,414 ETH as of October 4, applying MicroStrategy's Bitcoin treasury accumulation model to Ethereum.

crypto.title: Ethereum PropAMMs: Today and Tomorrow
crypto.summary: PropAMMs hold 5-10% of Ethereum DEX volume against 40% on Solana, with Fermi ($280M) and Metric ($178M) well behind Uniswap's $6B in the week of September 14-20.

crypto.title: Bitcoin Breaks Below $83,000 as Oil Jumps on Iran Strike-Plan Report
crypto.summary: Bitcoin fell to $82,800, breaking the technical level FxPro analysts identified as a trigger point below which sellers take control and prices could move toward $80,000.

it.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5
it.summary: Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest and cheapest small model to date, designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks such as summaries, database queries, and classifications. The new model costs roughly 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5 and is available across major cloud platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Alongside the launch, Anthropic halved cache read prices for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and introduced monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers.

it.title: Should the agent even look that up?
it.summary: Decision models can efficiently determine when AI agents need to retrieve long-term memory, reducing unnecessary context and token usage without sacrificing accuracy. Using a carefully designed classifier reduced injected context by 85% and eliminated five of eight memory calls.

it.title: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
it.summary: GitHub Copilot is introducing support for local inference models and sandboxed tool execution on Windows devices, coordinated automatically with cloud models through intelligent orchestration. To enable this, Microsoft AI developed a quantized local version of the coding-optimized MAI Code 1.1 Flash model running on NVIDIA RTX Spark hardware with unified memory. Additionally, Microsoft Execution Containers provide operating-system-level sandboxing to secure shell commands and local server interactions during agentic workflows.

it.title: SAP Just Added Stablecoin Settlement to the Software That Runs 84% of Global Commerce
it.summary: SAP has introduced SAP Pay, an ERP-level accounting upgrade embedded in SAP Cloud ERP that enables institutional stablecoin settlement in USDC and EURC. Developed in partnership with Tereina and Circle, the platform allows multinational corporations to settle invoices across 89 global payment corridors directly within their existing enterprise software workflows. The infrastructure relies on Circle's Arc blockchain and is supported by upcoming Joule AI agents designed to execute autonomous payments.

it.title: Building Windows for hybrid intelligence
it.summary: Microsoft has announced the expansion of Windows into a platform for hybrid intelligence, combining local AI processing with cloud capabilities and introducing enhanced security controls. The release includes generally available Microsoft Execution Containers for agent containment, new local model support via Windows ML and llama.cpp, and an expanded ecosystem of builder PCs and desktop supercomputers powered by NVIDIA technology.

it.title: AWS launches Strands Box, an open-source AI agent sandbox to prevent YOLO mode disasters
it.summary: The new solution integrates tools like the Dogwood Local Engine, Strands Shell, and Python interpreters to give the policy engine temporal awareness, enabling developers to monitor and restrict file deletions, API calls, and Slack postings based on prior actions.

hardware.title: TSMC's September sales surge year-over-year as AI drives chip demand
hardware.summary: TSMC reported revenue of $511.86 billion New Taiwan dollars for September, a 54.6% year-over-year increase. Demand for advanced AI chips, driven by customers like Nvidia and Apple, boosted sales. TSMC has also committed to using ASML's advanced lithography machines to enhance chip production.

hardware.title: Amazon builds its 1,000th Leo satellite at 27 a week, but only 396 are in orbit
hardware.summary: Amazon built its 1,000th Leo broadband satellite at its Kirkland, Washington plant, which took six months to produce its first 27 and now turns out 27 a week. It builds propulsion in-house and borrowed consumer electronics methods to cut tests that took weeks down to hours. The bottleneck is launch: only 396 are in orbit against 3,232 needed, and the Vulcan grounding and a New Glenn pad explosion cost Amazon FCC spectrum priority.

hardware.title: Anderon aims to industrialize quantum chip fabrication
hardware.summary: IEEE Spectrum examines the up-to-$1B CHIPS R&D award finalized for IBM spinoff Anderon in September. IBM is matching that funding with $1B, while Anderon uses a 300mm Albany line and plans foundry services and process design kits for outside developers. The challenge is repeatable fabrication, including tighter control of Josephson junctions, rather than simply adding wafer capacity.

hardware.title: Google open-sources ML Drift, a GPU engine that runs one shader set across OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and OpenGL ES
hardware.summary: Tensor virtualization decouples a tensor's logical layout from its physical GPU allocation, so one shader template replaces separate backend-specific codebases. For edge LLMs, ML Drift switches kernels between compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode, using a convolution-aligned KV cache layout and in-kernel activation quantization to skip memory roundtrips. It cut YouTube Shorts frame latency by up to 40%, and Google co-optimized it with Arm, Intel, and Qualcomm GPUs.

hardware.title: Supercapacitor cement is key to buildings that store their own power
hardware.summary: Scientists from the Harbin Institute of Technology developed a cement-based supercapacitor capable of powering small devices like LEDs. The device uses a 3D-printed electrode ink made from carbon nanotubes and cement, enabling fast energy discharge. Future research will enhance cold-weather performance, potentially allowing buildings to store energy and support smart environments.

hardware.title: Too many quantum startups, too little money to keep them alive
hardware.summary: Gartner predicts that over half of quantum startups will fail by 2030 due to a market unable to generate sufficient revenue. Despite this, companies are investing in quantum technologies for their potential business advantages, focusing on building expertise rather than waiting for technological maturity. The public sector and financial industries are expected to lead quantum computing investments, with spending reaching $245 million and $289 million by 2027 and 2028, respectively.

hardware.title: There's a hidden upside to the rampocalypse for Apple
hardware.summary: Apple gained a full percentage point in market share year-over-year as RAM price increases led to a 20% decrease in overall PC shipments. Despite this downturn, Apple was less affected than most competitors. With prices expected to worsen, Apple's resilience highlights its strong customer base willing to invest in new devices.

hardware.title: NVIDIA's Safety Stack for Physical AI
